Direction prediction remained near chance (macro F1 0.532), limited by the lack of samples in the HAMdb compounds that are marked as autophagy inhibitors (only 132 inhibitors). Taken together, these results suggest that binary structure-based classification can prioritize autophagy modulators, while transcriptome regression and structure-based direction prediction are not supported by current data.

item.title: A bipartite quantum-acoustic architecture stabilizes multi-exciton solitons at 323 K
SpectraFit-Core: a Rust-cored nonlinear curve-fitting library validated against the NIST Statistical Reference Datasets
item.description: Nonlinear least-squares fitting of parametric line shapes is routine in the analysis of spectra, and the analyst often knows relationships between the parameters before the fit starts, such as a shared width or a fixed intensity ratio. SpectraFit-Core is an open-source curve-fitting library in which this knowledge is part of the model. A model is a graph of named components, and each relationship is an expression edge on that graph, within one spectrum or across several spectra fitted jointly in one call. On a measured Fe L2,3 energy-loss spectrum, four such relationships leave the fitted values unchanged and make the edge-step amplitude 28 times more precise. Because the model is a description rather than code, the same graph can be fitted by other implementations and their parameters compared name by name. The parameters and standard errors of the library are checked against certified values: on 22 of the 27 nonlinear-regression problems of the NIST Statistical Reference Datasets, the least accurately recovered parameter agrees to more than six significant figures, and the standard errors agree nearly as well except on Lanczos1. Kernels, analytic Jacobians, and solver iteration run in compiled Rust behind a typed Python interface, which also makes the library faster than lmfit, SciPy, and JAX on its benchmark. A companion repository regenerates the results from the published release. SpectraFit-Core is released under the MIT license, distributed on PyPI and archived on Zenodo.

item.title: Generative discovery, symmetry-aware membership screening, and device-level evaluation of six-member-ring MoS2 polytypes
item.description: Six-membered-ring (SMR) inorganic materials were recently unified into a class, but the class-level perspective lacks two enabling tools: an operational test of “SMR-ness” and a path from newly generated crystals to device-level figures of merit. Here we couple conditional generative modelling (MatterGen; Mo–S, Ti–S, W–Se; 512 cells per system) to a novelty/stability funnel, a symmetry-aware membership checker that casts the SMR definition as three calibrated criteria (6/6 positives, 6/6 trap negatives), full DFT relaxation with composition-anchored hull analysis, and a contract-based device evaluation injecting literature-anchored OCV and diffusivity into an electrochemical cell model. The campaign maps the AA-stacked polytype manifold across five TMD chemistries, confirming 61 candidates (12 MoS2, 7 TiS2, 18 WSe2, 16 MoSe2, 8 NbS2; e.g. the MoS2 series P6̄m2, c = 7.1–40.8 Å, Ehull = 0.019–0.022 eV atom−1), 56 of them novel against every queried database. A dedicated spin cross-check (ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic and unpolarised initialisations) collapses to zero moments in every tested channel, and a three-probe stability screen (phonons, annealing dynamics, hull distance) shows the layered frameworks robust while the AA registry is metastable toward layer sliding, sharpening the synthesis list into kinetically stabilisable targets with two registry-robust entries. Two methodological findings transfer to any SMR screening effort: minimum-ring statistics collapse on TMD coordination (four-rings swallow six-rings), and membership is adjudicable only after relaxation. At the device end, material classes are discriminated by 0.639 V and polytypes by computed Li barriers (a 1.6× 108 diffusivity ratio separates fast from frozen at 0.5C); every number is traceable to a versioned experiment record.

item.title: Accelerating Catalyst Discovery with Artificial Intelligence Using Molecular Dual-Atom Site Catalysts as a Case Study
item.description: We test whether researchers can delegate the writing of a complete catalyst study to a large language model while retaining scientific judgment. Our case study concerns molecular dual-atom site catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction, where stabilizing an adsorbed intermediate can make its subsequent reduction less favorable. Using density functional theory calculations on 88 catalysts, we explain this balance through adsorption free energies and the overpotential volcano. We then use adsorbate specific ridge models to predict adsorption energies for 1,260 additional structures and identify candidates for further study. Among candidates with low predicted overpotentials, we find predominantly Fe adsorption centers, with separate structural patterns associated with S bridges and 1,2phenylenediamine. To communicate the reasoning behind these choices, we guided a large language model with explicit scientific writing instructions and refined its explanations through repeated scientific and editorial review. The resulting article is the demonstration: we delegate manuscript preparation while retaining responsibility for its scientific meaning. This approach to accelerating catalyst discovery with artificial intelligence offers researchers an opportunity to concentrate on scientific investigation while guiding how their results are communicated.

item.title: Mechanistic Insights into the Non-Equilibrium Synthesis of Highly Fluorinated Cation-Disordered Rock-Salt Cathodes: Solid-State Thermal vs. Mechanochemical Reactions
item.description: Fluorination is an effective strategy to improve the stability of high-capacity cation-disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes, yet incorporating substantial fluorine through conventional thermal synthesis remains challenging. Although mechanochemical milling enables highly fluorinated compositions, the reaction pathways underlying this capability remain poorly understood. This study compares the thermal and mechanochemical synthesis of Li2Mn0.5Ti0.5O2F from identical precursors using in situ thermal and custom-made quasi in situ mechanochemical synchrotron X-ray diffraction. Thermal synthesis proceeds through a Ti-rich DRX intermediate followed by Mn incorporation. Subsequent LiF incorporation coincides with MnO segregation, while further heating induces phase decomposition and substantial fluorine loss. In contrast, mechanochemical milling generates a transient amorphous intermediate that coexists with Ti-rich DRX during progressive MnO incorporation and subsequently transforms into highly fluorinated DRX. Elemental analysis combined with 19F solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance shows estimated fluorine contents of 1.00–1.06 F per formula unit of DRX after mechanochemical synthesis, compared with 0.32–0.41 after thermal synthesis. These findings support an amorphous-mediated pathway for accommodating Mn and F within metastable DRX, highlighting control over transient intermediates as a strategy for accessing highly fluorinated oxyfluoride cathodes.

item.title: Toward Interpretable Graph-Based Machine Learning for Combustion Kinetic Model Generation
item.description: This work presents an atom-conserving and interpretable graph neural network (GNN) for combustion kinetic model generation, where atoms are represented as nodes, covalent bonds are represented as edges, and reactions are represented as bond-rearrangement operations. Its artificial-intelligence (AI) contribution is a reaction generator that extends a standard Graph Isomorphism Network with Edges (GINE) architecture through reaction-context embeddings, reaction branching & third-body reaction inputs, Arrhenius-rate-parameter prediction, pairwise decoding, and stochastic inference over evolving reactant pools. Trained on the Li–Dryer hydrogen combustion kinetic model (8 species and 21 reactions), the GNN reproduces trained chemistry and generates element-balanced new reactions and intermediate species outside the training dataset, many of which have experimental analogues. When trained on a subset of the Li–Dryer dataset, the model recovered most held-out reactions and revealed relationships between samples (reactions) in the model’s latent space. The results suggest that the model learns transferable local reaction structures and generates valid species and reactions. As with any reaction generators, the generated reaction models require thermochemical and kinetic verification; the intended engineering application is low-cost reaction-pathway exploration for new fuels and prioritization of experiments and first-principles calculations to develop new combustion kinetic models.

item.title: What a low-bias filter leaves out: measured performance on the excluded negatives of a drug–target interaction benchmark
item.description: Eligibility rules define which interactions contribute to a benchmark score. The low-bias BindingDB benchmark retains a drug only when it has both positive and negative labels, excluding measured inactive pairs involving drugs without a measured active. We reconstructed this rule in a declared BindingDB population and evaluated retained and excluded negatives against the same positive reference. After cleaning and an additional connectivity-overlap restriction, the excluded region contained 78.4% of the measured negative pairs. DrugBAN and MolTrans were trained in three evaluation designs with five seeds; a released BioT5 checkpoint was evaluated on its published split. Across these evaluations, pooled AUROC was 0.072–0.136 lower on excluded negatives. Lower performance also occurred within proteins with sufficient observations in both regions. DrugBAN remained ahead of MolTrans, but the change in their advantage depended on aggregation: it generally increased under pooled AUROC, whereas equalprotein weighting produced smaller or oppositely directed changes. Cross-protein comparisons accounted for approximately 99.8–99.9% of pooled AUROC's pair-comparison weight. The closer BioT5–DrugBAN comparison additionally depended on scoring convention. These results measure regional performance differences, conditional on the chosen positive reference; they do not estimate a causal filter effect or deployment performance. Benchmark reports should specify eligibility, coverage at the evaluated unit, metric aggregation, and performance on excluded regions where labels are available.

item.title: Fabrication and Microstructural Analysis of ZnO and In2O3 MOS Thin Film Sensors with Embedded Microheaters for Methane Sensing
item.description: Methane detection is essential for both environmental monitoring and industrial safety due to its greenhouse impact and explosive potential. Conventional sensing approaches, such as electrochemical, infrared, and catalytic bead sensors, are limited by stability and sensitivity constraints. Metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors, particularly those based on ZnO and In2O3, provide an attractive alternative owing to their stability, high sensitivity, compactness, and fabrication compatibility. In this work, compact MOS chip sensors were developed using a six-layer architecture that integrates a microheater for localized thermal control. Thin films of ZnO and In2O3 were deposited via magnetron sputtering with photolithographically defined geometries, followed by annealing under inert gas conditions. Microstructural and surface morphological characterization was performed using atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). Results revealed that ZnO films undergo significant surface restructuring upon annealing, exhibiting increased roughness, grain coarsening, and oxygen vacancy formation, whereas In2O3 retained compact morphology and stoichiometric stability. These findings establish a sensitivity–stability trade-off between the two materials, with ZnO showing higher surface activity favourable for methane adsorption, and In2O3 offering reproducibility and long-term stability.

item.title: Chemical Representation Dependence of Quinone Reduction Energetics: Site-Specific Limits of Methylthio Surrogates for Cysteine-Derived Conjugates
item.description: Methylthio substituents are compact models for larger sulfur-linked quinone conjugates, yet their fidelity for calculated one-electron reduction-energy shifts is uncertain. We audited a historical survey of 38 methylthio attachment sites in 26 quinones; four source-energy outputs remain unreconciled, leaving 34 archive-corroborated site shifts across 25 parents. In a historical matched comparison of ten SMe and N-acetylcysteine methyl ester-derived (AcCysOMe) conjugate models, the original median absolute mismatch was 0.175900 eV. An explicitly retrospective, source-corroborated eightsite subset retained a median mismatch of 0.162917 eV, above the prespecified 0.05 eV screening tolerance, with category agreement of 1/3 among decisive SMe cases. Four separately conformercorrected case studies included opposite-sign shifts for benz[a]anthracene-3,4-dione and its 7-methyl analogue. An alternative-functional PBE0-D4 fixed-geometry analysis retained both numerical sign differences, although the 7-methyl analogue's AcCysOMe shift (−0.037065 eV) was near zero under the original category rule. item.title: Pyrrolidinium-Assisted Proton and Cation Exchange Enables Near-Quantitative Rare Earth Extraction from Synthetic NdFeB Leachate
item.description: Diglycolamide (DGA) extractants offer strong affinity for rare-earth elements (REEs), tunable coordination, and phosphorus-free chemistry. Incomplete use of their molar capacity limits extractant utilization efficiency (EUE), while low distribution ratios (D) require larger organic-phase volumes. Ionic liquids (ILs) can stabilize DGA–REE complexes and modify extraction pathways, with proton exchange reported in some imidazolium ILs and IL-mediated cation or anion exchange in others. Combining exchange pathways within a single system could improve extraction and EUE, but this remains underexplored. Screening five ILs with N,N-dioctyldiglycolamic acid (DODGAA) identified [C2mpyrr][NTf2] as the best-performing formulation, outperforming the tested pyridinium- and imidazolium-based ILs and achieving an Nd3+ distribution ratio of approximately 7,000 at an organic-to-aqueous volume ratio of 0.1 with near-quantitative extraction. Slope analysis (~3.3), proton balance (~1 H+ per Nd3+), and aqueous 1H NMR support coupled proton and IL-cation exchange. The maximum EUE of 17.0% is comparable to several organophosphorus extractants. In synthetic NdFeB leachate, Nd3+ and Dy3+ were extracted at >99%, with low boron transfer and iron removed by hydroxide precipitation. Over five extraction–stripping cycles, the organic phase retained ~73% of its initial extraction efficiency, limited by incomplete single-stage stripping. Pyrrolidinium-assisted coupled exchange offers an efficient route to REE extraction.

item.title: Spatially Separated NO Capture and Hydrogenation for NH3 Synthesis from O2-Containing Streams
item.description: The selective conversion of nitric oxide (NO) in combustion flue gases to ammonia (NH3) is a promising strategy for sustainable nitrogen management. However, this conversion remains challenging in O2-containing exhaust gases because coexisting O2 strongly inhibits catalytic hydrogenation. Here, we developed a tandem NO capture and hydrogenation system for NH3 production from O2-containing streams. Various adsorbents were examined for NO capture in the presence of O2, and Li-impregnated β zeolite with 1.2 wt% Li, denoted as Li(1.2)/β, was selected as a representative adsorbent owing to its high NOx adsorption capacity. In situ IR spectroscopy showed that NOx species formed from NO + O2 on Li(1.2)/β were mainly present as [NO+][NO2] adducts, which subsequently desorbed as NO2 upon heating. By coupling the Li(1.2)/β-based temperature-swing adsorption unit, operated between 30 and 200 °C, with a downstream Cu(5)/CeO2 hydrogenation reactor operated at 450 °C, the tandem system maintained an NH3 yield of 55–60% during a 7 h cyclic operation. These results demonstrate the feasibility of spatially separated NO capture and downstream NOx hydrogenation for converting NO in O2-containing streams into a valuable nitrogen resource.

item.title: Cholesterol-Dependent Membrane Fluidity in Sindbis Virus Governs Viral Particle Stability and Infectivity
item.description: Cholesterol is a key biomolecule that regulates lipid bilayer fluidity, and cholesterol-rich domains in host cells and virions are critical for virion entry and egress. Here, using Alphavirus Sindbis virus (SINV) as a model, we combine new experimental methods and single-particle biological characterization to revisit how envelope cholesterol affects particle stability and the biological consequences for infectivity. To this end, we generated two SINV populations with a 3-fold difference in envelope cholesterol levels (SINVLC and SINVHC) to assess how cholesterol affects SINV stability and infectivity. Transmission electron microscopy and dynamic light scattering showed minimal differences in morphology and size, indicating that cholesterol minimally alters virion structure. Electrochemical measurements between SINVLC and SINVHC particles revealed similar Zeta Potentials (ζ-potential ~ -31 mV), which implies that the surface distribution of the E1-E2 glycoprotein heterotrimers within the envelope is cholesterol-independent. Titer measurements showed that SINVHC retains nearly an order of magnitude more infectious particles than SINVLC when pre-exposed to 30 minutes of thermal stress, corresponding to a 1.25-fold faster decay rate for the low-cholesterol virions, with SINVLC and SINVHC showing values of 0.34/min and 0.27/min, respectively. Single-particle fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy analysis using the fluidity-sensitive dye DI-8-ANEPPS revealed a statistically significant increase (≥ 0.2 ns; p < 0.0001) in photon arrival times in the SINVHC population, indicating that elevated cholesterol enhances membrane rigidity. Because virion size and ζ-potential remained unchanged while fluorescence lifetimes increased with cholesterol level, these findings indicate that membrane fluidity is the primary parameter governing viral stability and subsequent infectivity.

item.title: PARAMAGNETIC SUPRAMOLECULAR POLYMERS OF METAL-METAL BONDED DIRUTHENIUM COMPLEXES
Cationic surfactant-modified cotton and cotton/polyester textile-derived biochar for hexavalent chromium removal via ion-exchange
item.description: Biochar derived from textile waste presents an opportunity in the circular economy for contaminant remediation from industrial wastewater. In this study, biochars derived from cotton and cotton-polyester blended textiles were assessed for the removal of the toxic and pervasive aqueous contaminant, hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)). Unmodified textile-derived biochars exhibited some adsorption capacity for Cr(VI) under environmentally relevant pH conditions, but removal improved substantially once modified with the cationic surfactant cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB). Adsorption experiments conducted at 50–100 mg/L as Cr showed equilibrium capacities of about 1.6–2.0 mg Cr/g BC for unmodified biochars, increasing to 10–15 mg Cr/g BC for CTAB-modified materials, with rapid adsorption in the first 5 minutes. Maximum adsorption capacity for CTAB-modified cotton and cotton-polyester biochar prepared at 450 oC was determined to be 72 and 32 mg Cr/g BC, respectively, comparable to established adsorbents. Adsorption-desorption experiments conducted using low (10 mM NaCl) and high (500 mM NaCl) ionic strength showed apparent anion exchange capacities of ~0.08 to 0.09 meq/g, suggesting that chromium retention involves ion exchange with CTAB-derived quaternary ammonium sites in addition to electrostatic attraction. Similar adsorption behavior between feedstocks suggests that surfactant modification played a larger role in overall performance than feedstock composition. These findings demonstrate that textile-derived biochar can be engineered through surfactant modification to enhance the removal efficiency of industrially-relevant anionic contaminants like Cr(VI), supporting their potential use as low-cost sorbents for industrial wastewater treatment.

item.title: Data-efficient molecular and nanoparticle design via fine-tuned large language models
item.description: Designing molecules with prescribed properties is central to pharmaceutical and materials innovation, but vast chemical design spaces make development lengthy and costly. Generative artificial intelligence can accelerate molecular discovery, but its deployment in many real-world domains remains limited by the need for large task-specific training datasets. To enable generative design when property-labeled data are scarce, we present a data-efficient foundation-model adaptation strategy combining complementary positive and negative property prompts with parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Generated molecules are then ranked by molecular graph-kernel Gaussian process regression for structure-aware prioritization. In a controlled computational setting, the platform generated candidates with novel scaffolds satisfying multiple design objectives, including predicted target binding, synthesizability, and drug-likeness. Although only a few hundred training molecules per target met all three criteria, the model generated thousands of new molecules matching the desired profiles. For prospective validation, we applied the model to nanoparticle design, a domain of high clinical potential but limited excipient diversity. Fine-tuning on only 1,521 labeled drug-excipient pairs - including just 139 nanoparticle-forming examples identified new nanoparticle-forming excipients for the anticancer drug sorafenib. The model proposed lithocholic acid and the sorafenib metabolite M6, and experiments confirmed that both form stable sorafenib nanoparticles with high encapsulation efficiency and increased in vitro potency. These findings show that foundation-model fine-tuning with complementary prompts and graph-based prioritization enables data-efficient molecular design in low-data chemical domains.

item.title: Resolving the Methanol-Promoting Alloy–Oxide Ensemble in Pd–Zn/C Catalysts for CO2 Hydrogenation
item.description: Pd–Zn bimetallic catalysts are a promising alternative to traditional Cu-based systems for the hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol. Yet a complete understanding of their structure-activity relationships has been hindered by methodological limitations, such as high-temperature synthesis and the use of bulk characterization techniques. Here, we use an inert graphitic carbon support to prepare a Pd–Zn/C catalyst library with systematically varied Zn:Pd ratio and pre-treatment temperature. In situ Pd and Zn K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), coupled with multivariate curve resolution, resolves the coexisting Pd–Zn and Zn-derived oxide components, including Pd-rich FCC α-PdZny, ordered tetragonal Zn-rich β1-PdZnz, crystalline ZnO, and disordered ZnOx. The components identified by XAS provide a reference database for the detailed chemical speciation across the catalyst library. In situ XAS showed that catalysts pre-treated in H2 at 250-450 °C do not restructure during catalysis, and therefore it is sufficient to analyze their structure before catalysis to uncover structure-activity correlations. Combined with kinetic measurements and statistical correlation analysis, this framework identifies the structural motifs associated with methanol and CO formation. Methanol productivity is linked to the coexistence of ordered tetragonal β1-PdZnz (z > 1) and disordered ZnOx, whereas CO forms across a broader range of Pd-containing bimetallic environments. In situ restructuring experiments for the catalysts pre-treated at mild conditions (50 °C) further show that the hydride-forming FCC α-PdZny phase acts as a precursor that can evolve toward the more methanol-selective β1-phase to form an active interface under catalytic conditions in the presence of Zn oxide. These results resolve the methanol-promoting alloy–oxide ensemble in Pd–Zn catalysts and show that selective methanol synthesis depends on stabilizing the appropriate local oxidic environment at the alloy boundary, rather than simply maximizing Zn loading or alloy fraction.

item.title: Vibrational Excitation of Water Drives Proton Reactivity with Native Proteins During Mid-Infrared Laser Desorption Coupled to Mass Spectrometry.
item.description: We discovered a vibrational-excitation-driven proton reactivity between proteins and their surrounding aqueous environment during mid-infrared laser Desorption by Impulsive Vibrational Excitation (DIVE). We show that this process, when coupled directly to high resolution mass spectrometry (MS) without secondary ionization sources, produces intact gas-phase ions of proteins retaining their compact conformations. The unexpected multiple protonation states of protein ions are generated through a series of concerted proton transfer processes to protein surface residues. We propose that laser-induced ionization via DIVE is facilitated by sub-nanosecond transient superheating and Grotthuss proton hopping processes. By coupling to high-resolution MS, protein ionization via DIVE opens up an avenue for chemical and structural characterization of proteins and their complexes directly from aqueous and physiological buffer environments.

item.title: A hydrochromic porous aromatic framework for self-reporting, high-capacity atmospheric water harvesting
item.description: Atmospheric water harvesting materials are typically optimised for sorption performance alone, despite the practical importance of monitoring sorbent loading. Here, we report a hydrochromic porous aromatic framework that integrates water capture and self-reporting within a single adaptive material. Sulfonation of PAF-1 affords the hydrophilic framework PAF-1-S that adsorbs 0.18 g·g-1 of water at only 10% RH and reaches 1.87 g·g-1 at 90% RH, combining exceptional low-humidity capture with the highest total capacity among the porous sorbents surveyed here. Water adsorption simultaneously induces a reversible, graded colour change, enabling direct visualisation of sorbent loading without external sensing hardware. Spectroscopic analysis indicates that this response arises from hydration-driven acid–base equilibria within the modified framework. Combined with rapid sorption kinetics, low-temperature regeneration and robust cycling stability, these findings establish responsive porous adsorbents as a strategy for intelligent sorption materials.

item.title: Photocatalyst-Free Visible-Light-Induced Trifluoroalkylation of Electron-Deficient Heteroaromatics via a Three-Component Minisci-Type Reaction.
item.description: The combination of electron-poor heterocycles and trifluoromethyl motifs is widely found in pharmaceuticals, making the development of methods for the simultaneous introduction of these two features highly desirable. Herein, we report a fast, acid-free, metal-free, photocatalyst-free, and operationally simple multicomponent approach for the trifluoroalkylation of electron-poor heterocycles under open-air conditions. The method relies on the ability of trifluoromethyl thianthrenium triflate to generate CF3 radicals and proceeds through a polarity-reversal cascade strategy employing electron-rich alkenes as linkers. A broad range of alkenes and heterocycles was evaluated, and the chemo-and regioselectivity of the process were thoroughly investigated. Furthermore, mechanistic studies revealed that multiple pathways contribute to the formation of the desired products.

item.title: One-Pot Synthesis of Oxazolines from Carboxylic Acids and Amino Alcohols using Phosphorus(V) Catalysis
item.description: Oxazolines are important heterocycles for a range of industrial applications, and yet their synthesis from simple carboxylic acid and amino alcohol substrates requires multiple steps and stoichiometric reagents. Here, we demonstrate the one-pot direct synthesis using a bifunctional boronic acid/phosphorus(V) catalyst that is shown to catalyze both the amidation and cyclodehydration steps. Different classes of carboxylic acid coupling partners are surveyed, the mechanism for cyclodehydration investigated, and a variety of 2-substituted oxazolines prepared without the addition of stoichiometric reagents.

item.title: Ion Pairing and Electrochemical Behavior of Al(OTf)3 in Propylene Carbonate Bilal Overton
item.description: The development of practical aluminum-ion batteries requires electrolytes capable of stabilizing multivalent aluminum species while maintaining sufficient ionic conductivity and electrochemical activity. Here, we investigate aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTf)3) dissolved in propylene carbonate (PC) as a potential halide-free aluminum electrolyte using a combined computational and experimental approach. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to optimize coordination structures and predict speciation, redox potentials, and vibrational signatures of solvated aluminum complexes. Cyclic voltammetry reveals electrochemical activity with a reduction onset near 0 V versus Al/Al3+, consistent with computational predictions. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy indicates significant ionic association between aluminum and triflate anions, suggesting the coexistence of free and coordinated species in solution. Scanning electron microscopy of copper substrates after chronoamperometric deposition shows surface features consistent with metal deposition, while X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirms the presence of aluminum-containing species. The electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of approximately 5.4 mS cm-1 at ~0.6 M. These results demonstrate that Al(OTf)3/PC solutions support electrochemical activity of aluminum species but exhibit strong ion association, highlighting key challenges and opportunities for halide-free aluminum battery electrolytes.

item.title: Discovery of Nanomolar CDK2 Inhibitors Using Boltz-2
item.description: The computational design of small-molecule ligands for pharmaceutical targets has historically been hindered by a strict trade-off between screening throughput and predictive accuracy. While next-generation cofolding affinity models like Boltz-2 hold immense promise for bridging this gap, their utility in prospective medicinal chemistry campaigns remains largely unexplored. To date, virtual screens leveraging these models have been overwhelmingly restricted to standard commercial catalogs, leaving their capacity to navigate novel, synthetically tailored chemical spaces unevaluated. Here, we present a novel hit discovery platform that integrates Boltz-2’s affinity module with a custom screening space of stereochemically complex tetrahydroquinolines, accessed efficiently via a single-step multicomponent approach. Boltz-2 successfully guided both the initial high-throughput virtual screening of these targeted scaffolds and subsequent hit optimization, rapidly yielding nanomolar inhibitors of cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2).

item.title: Sterically Shielded Cations Decouple Ion-Exchange Capacity from Water Uptake in Anion Exchange Membranes
item.description: Anion exchange membranes (AEMs) for electrochemical devices must combine high ion-exchange capacity (IEC) with controlled hydration and dimensional stability. Water uptake is commonly rationalized in terms of IEC and intrinsic cation hydrophilicity, but this picture fails when the cationic site is locally shielded by the polymer architecture. Using the poly(bis-imidazolium) ionene Aemion+® as a model backbone-embedded AEM, we find that it absorbs only ~40% of the water taken up by pendant-cation analogues at matched IEC, reversing the trend expected from solution thermodynamics, which identifies its embedded dimethylimidazolium cation as the more hydrophilic one. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations reveal that adjacent aromatic rings create a three-dimensional steric envelope around the embedded cation, reducing first-shell water coordination by 69% and chloride coordination by 62% relative to the free cation in solution. Restricted access to the cation persists for the membrane in hydroxide form. To separate cation chemistry from architecture, we synthesize poly(phenylene oxide) (PPO) membranes bearing four pendant cations—tetramethylammonium (TMA), dimethylimidazolium (DMIm), piperidinium (Pip), and pyrrolidinium (Mpy)—at matched IEC and find that PPO–TMA and PPO–DMIm have indistinguishable hydration despite the substantially higher intrinsic hydrophilicity of DMIm⁺ in solution, with all four cations falling within a narrow hydration window. These results establish local steric accessibility — the ability of water and counterions to occupy the cation's first solvation shell — as a controlling descriptor for AEM hydration. Engineering cation accessibility therefore offers a molecular design strategy for high-IEC AEMs with controlled hydration and swelling.

item.title: A Novel Reactive Incipient Wetness Impregnation Assisted by H2O2 for Vanadium Catalysts: the Case of V/Silicalite-1 zeolites in Oxidative Propane Dehydrogenation
item.description: Metal deposition in zeolites is often interpreted using concepts developed for relatively open support surfaces, overlooking the consequences of precursor transport and deposition within confined microporous environments. Here, we introduce an H2O2-mediated reactive impregnation strategy for supported vanadium catalysts reactive vanadium impregnation mediated by H2O2 and that avoids organics complexing agents (carbon-free) exploiting vanadium-peroxo chemistry to dissolve in situ the precursor into smaller complexed soluble species and modify its interaction with Silicalite-1. The resulting catalyst displayed still detectable vanadium aggregates compared with conventional impregnation. The materials tested under oxidative propane dehydrogenation exhibited comparable catalytic activity (slightly higher) but improved stability during repeated reaction-regeneration cycling. The in situ coke accumulation within a cycle was tracked in the intermediary regeneration steps by using online MS, and showed similar amounts for both preparation routes, suggesting that carbon deposition is governed predominantly by the structural and pore-capacity characteristics of Silicalite-1. Structural characterization revealed distinct vanadium-support interactions in the H2O2-assisted materials, while microscopy and H2-TPR indicated different evolution of the support and vanadium phase during cycling. Under representative OPDH conditions, the H2O2-assisted catalyst reached 41% propane conversion and 90% propylene selectivity, with a 30% lower deactivation rate over ten cycles. A Dioxasilepane-Functionalized Styrenic Monomer as a Platform for Novel Silicon-Containing Polystyrenes
item.description: A dioxasilepane-derived styrenic monomer, 2,4,4,7,7-pentamethyl-2-(4-vinylphenyl)-1,3,2-dioxasilepane (St-Si(pan)Me), is introduced as the first polymerizable representative of the recently developed Si(pan) platform, a seven-membered cyclic dialkoxysilane motif combining high stability with controllable silicon reactivity. The monomer combines the exceptional kinetic stability of the seven-membered cyclic dialkoxysilane with a polymerizable styrenic functionality, enabling direct incorporation of the Si(pan) motif into polystyrene-based polymers and materials. Following multigram-scale synthesis, the compatibility of St-Si(pan)Me with conventional free-radical polymerization was systematically investigated. Among the investigated polymerization temperatures (70 - 90 °C), 90 °C provided the best balance between molar-mass distribution, structural fidelity, thermal stability, and photophysical performance while fully preserving the integrity of the Si(pan) framework. Beyond free radical polymerization, Reversible Addition-Fragmentation Chain-Transfer (RAFT) polymerization showed compatibility with controlled radical polymerization, while preliminary emulsion polymerization revealed distinct behavior under aqueous conditions, suggesting opportunities for future siloxane network formation. Copolymerization with styrene afforded silicon-functionalized copolymers with tuneable compositions and systematically adjustable molecular, thermal, and photophysical properties. Comprehensive characterization by various techniques confirmed successful incorporation of the Si(pan) functionality throughout the polymer series. This work establishes St-Si(pan)Me as a versatile platform monomer that expands the toolbox of silicon-functionalized styrenes and provides access to a new class of thermally robust and intrinsically luminescent silicon-containing polystyrenes.

item.title: Conditional latent distillation enables controllable molecular generation in data-limited soft materials
item.description: De novo molecular generation is particularly difficult when materials-specific datasets are too small to support reliable training of a new generative backbone. We develop a framework for controllable molecular generation based on conditional latent distillation and chemistryconstrained construction. A variational autoencoder (VAE) pretrained on more than 20,000 polymer molecules supplies a starting molecular representation, reducing reliance on training a new generator from approximately 1,600 surfactant or 200 anion-exchange-membrane (AEM) records. A compact conditional student learns to predict teacher latent coordinates from molecular descriptors and property-associated inputs, while molecular exploration and chemistry-aware editing govern which candidate structures are constructed and retained. In the primary surfactant application, Bayesian optimization produced 841 cleaned novel structures and retained 118, compared with 205 and 15 from nearest-neighbor exploration under equal 20,000-attempt mutation budgets. An independent distillation-guided teacher-latent retrieval benchmark yielded 2.32 more retained candidates per request than anchor-count-matched random selection (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.78–2.86). The conditional mapping also reduced teacher-coordinate prediction error by 40.3% and decoderdistribution divergence by 59.1% relative to the strongest tested regression baselines, validating the distillation-based interface. Molecular dynamics characterized selected surfactants at a water–decane interface. We then applied the chemistry-constrained construction and screening workflow to AEM-related building blocks, obtaining 125 screened candidates and assessing selected cations in water. These results demonstrate controllable molecular exploration and structural selection in data-limited settings, without claiming experimentally verified control of final materials properties.

item.title: Synthesis of Leaching-Proof Single-Site Catalysts Based on Metallolinker MOFs
item.description: The creation of single-site catalysts, for which all active sites have the same structure, is a key goal in contemporary heterogeneous catalysis. Many MOF linkers present well-defined binding sites for transition metals and may thus provide access to single-site catalysts. Depending on how the metal is introduced into the linker-based binding site, however, additional undesired species such as pore-confined nanoparticles or node-bound metal centers may be formed that can be difficult to locate. Here, we introduce catalytic interrogation as a diagnostic workflow for identifying the types of active sites that contribute to the catalytic activity observed for MOF catalysts. Using a suite of MOFs with porphyrin linkers as a case study, we combine catalytic interrogation with extensive electron microscopy to shed light on the rhodium-based active sites present in the MOF. We show that for strongly coordinating binding sites that furnish leaching-proof MOF-based catalysts, post-synthetic metalation carries a significant risk of undesired nanoparticle incorporation. MOF assembly from metalated linkers, on the other hand, generates MOFs that behave as single-site catalysts.

item.title: An open-source electrosynthesis platform for reaction screening enables a nickel-catalyzed electroreductive aryl cyanation
item.description: The application of electrochemistry to synthetic organic chemistry has resulted in the development of more efficient and sustainable synthesis methodologies. However, the costs and technical burdens of electrochemical instrumentation impose barriers towards the wider adoption of electrochemistry. Herein, we report a modular, open-source platform for electrosynthesis screening built around a low-cost miniaturized potentiostat. The platform supports electrosynthesis and electroanalytic methods, and its open design readily allows for customization. We demonstrate this utility of the platform by the development of a zinc-free, nickel-catalyzed reductive cyanation of aryl bromides with an electrophilic cyanating agent (2-methyl-2-phenylmalononitrile, MPMN). Replacing stoichiometric zinc reductant with a sacrificial tertiary amine allows the cyanation of aryl bromides incompatible with the original zinc-based conditions. In addition, acetonitrile can be used in place of typical hazardous amide solvents. This work provides a blueprint for non-expert practitioners to integrate electrochemistry as an accessible and affordable technique in their research programs.

item.title: Picking a Pucker: Excited-State Charge Redistribution Navigates the BN-Reshaped Conical-Intersection Landscape in Azaborine Photochemistry
item.description: Photoexcited benzene yields multiple isomers, whereas its BN isostere 1,2-azaborine selectively forms BN-Dewar benzene (BN-DB), despite both decaying through ringpuckered S1/S0 conical intersections (CIs). This selectivity is puzzling given that BNinduced asymmetry in 1,2-azaborine creates six distinct puckering sites and potentially multiple CIs, yet only a single photoproduct is observed. Here, we map the S1/S0 CI landscape of 1,2-azaborine using CASSCF and XMS-CASPT2 and identify eight N-, B-, and C-puckered CIs that open channels to various isomers including BN-DB and BN-benzvalene (BN-BV). BN incorporation therefore does not remove the excitedstate pathways of benzene but multiplies them. Of these CIs, only the N-puckered CIs leading to BN-DB lie below the S1 minimum, a preference we trace to S1 N→B charge redistribution. We then examine whether structural modifications that alter this redistribution can change CI accessibility, considering CH3 and F substitution and changes in B and N positions. Notably, 1,4-azaborine exhibits a qualitative shift from N→B to C→B charge redistribution. Consistently, C-and B-puckered CIs lie below the S1 minimum and may provide access to BN-BV, a versatile synthetic intermediate currently obtained through two photochemical steps. Together, these results suggest that S1 charge redistribution may be a key lever for steering azaborine photochemistry and for designing more direct routes to BN-BV.

item.title: Chiral Organic Single Crystals as a Platform for Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity
item.description: The chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect has attracted increasing attention for its unique ability to generate spin-polarized currents without magnetic components, with promising applications in spintronics, optoelectronics, and electrocatalysis. Although a wide range of chiral materials have been demonstrated to exhibit the CISS effect, most reported systems are based on amorphous films, self-assembled monolayers, or supramolecular assemblies, where structural disorder and aggregative traps compromise reliable evaluation of the CISS effect and obscure the structure-property relationship. Here, we overcome these limitations by constructing high-quality single crystals of chiral BN-embedded double helicenes, which feature a rigid chiral backbone and ordered molecular packing. Using magnetic conductive atomic force microscopy, we show that the single-crystal platform yields significantly improved current uniformity and measurement reproducibility compared with spin-coated thin films. Taking advantage of this enhanced reliability, we systematically investigated spin-selective transport in single crystals with thicknesses ranging from 18 to 330 nm. The spin polarization initially increases rapidly with crystal thickness, reaches a broad maximum, and remains pronounced over transport distances of up to 330 nm. This thickness-dependent behavior provides direct evidence for the cumulative spinselective transport along the long-range ordered structure, thereby distinguishing intrinsic bulk spin polarization from interfacial contributions. Our results thus establish chiral organic single crystals as a robust platform for investigating the CISS effect and unveiling clear structureproperty correlations.

item.title: Spectroscopic–Catalytic Onset Decoupling in Energy Electrocatalysis: Evidence, Mechanistic Hypotheses and Research Priorities from 250 Studies
item.description: Spectroelectrochemical methods can be used to reveal the chemistry that governs energy conversion and storage at operating interfaces. The review represents 250 primary studies that employed in situ or operando spectroscopy across carbon dioxide reduction, oxygen evolution, hydrogen evolution, battery interfaces and organic electronics. Three findings stand out. First, only five studies in the entire corpus provide paired surface and bulk onset potentials and these reveal offsets from zero to nearly 300 mV. Second, the magnitude of this offset tracks the binding strength of the catalytic intermediate rather than the prominence of its spectroscopic signature. Third, dynamic surface reconstruction creates active phases that differ from the as-prepared material in 147 of 250 systems. The central construct that emerges is onset decoupling: spectroscopic detection of an intermediate does not guarantee catalytic turnover, because binding energetics and site density govern whether accumulated species convert to products. This construct predicts that catalysts with strong intermediate binding will show large offsets and poor activity, while weak binding will produce coupled onsets and high activity.

item.title: Self-Sustained Sabatier Reaction via Submerged Photosynthesis
item.description: CO2 methanation is a promising route for carbon utilization, yet conventional processes remain constrained by their reliance on externally supplied H2 and specialized catalysts. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces a self-sustained Sabatier reaction based on the submerged photosynthesis of crystallites (SPSC). In this single aqueous system, metallic Fe and Mg powders react with carbonated water to generate H2 and CH4 near room temperature without an added methanation catalyst. Light irradiation accelerates the production of both gases. CH4 production scales approximately in proportion with H2 generation across diverse reaction conditions, with both gases exhibiting similar apparent activation energies. During the reaction, plate-like FeCO3 forms on the Fe surface, while Mg addition modifies this carbonate structure to enhance relative CH4 formation at longer reaction times. Scavenger experiments confirm the pivotal role of electron transfer in gas production. These results demonstrate that metal oxidation, electron transfer, and surface-bound carbonate reactions drive SPSC-methanation, successfully integrating in situ H2 generation, CH4 formation, and metal carbonate crystallization without external H2 input.

item.title: Structural pillar effect of Sn substitution in SrFe1‒xSnxO3‒δ catalysts for oxidative decomposition of 1,2-dichloroethane
item.description: Chlorination-induced structural degradation limits the durability of perovskite catalysts for the oxidative decomposition of chlorinated organic compounds. Here, a series of SrFe1−xSnxO3−δ (x = 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.0) was investigated for oxidation of 1,2-dichloroethane (1,2-DCE), with emphasis on the relationship between activity, structural stability and regenerability. Partial Sn substitution improved light-off performance relative to SrFeO3−δ, whereas SrSnO3 exhibited little catalytic activity. Although SrFe0.50Sn0.50O3−δ gave the highest conversion during temperature-programmed oxidation, SrFe0.25Sn0.75O3−δ (SFSO75) exhibited a more favorable balance between activity and structural stability. Independent exposure tests to CO2 and HCl revealed that Sn substitution enhanced resistance to carbonate and chloride formation, particularly after oxidative pretreatment. Under a dry reaction feed at 450 °C, SFSO75 retained approximately 40% conversion of 1,2-DCE after 12 h, exceeding that of unsubstituted SrFeO3−δ. Calcination of spent SFSO75 in air effectively restored its perovskite structure, and the regenerated catalyst maintained conversion at approximately 60% during a subsequent reaction of 12 h despite its lower surface area compared with the fresh catalyst. These results demonstrate the roles of Sn in enhancing activity and stabilizing and regenerating the perovskite structure as an effective approach to sustaining the performance of strontium ferrate for 1,2-DCE oxidation. Furthermore, with cofeeding 2.7% water vapor, fresh SFSO75 maintained conversion near 70% over 12 h and largely preserved the perovskite structure.

item.title: Quantum Coherence in Guest-Controlled Endohedral Fullerenes: Hierarchical Equations of Motion and a Neural-Network Model.
item.description: Light-harvesting efficiency hinges on how long an excitation stays coherent, yet in natural antennae the environment that destroys that coherence, the protein scaffold, cannot be redesigned at will. Here we invert the architecture and place the bath inside the chromophore: a C60 cage acts as the absorber while an encapsulated guest (CH4, N2, O2 or H2O) supplies a tunable internal environment. Combining B3LYP/6-31G* excitation energies, transition-electrostatic-potential (TrESP) couplings and hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM), we find that the choice of guest alone dictates the character of the dynamics. The guest acts through three parameters: the excitonic coupling to the neighbouring cage, the shift of the cage excitation energy and the reorganisation energy (λ). The damping of quantum beats grows in proportion to λ, coherent exchange gives way to incoherent hopping once λkBT/ℏγ becomes comparable to the coupling, and the guest-induced shifts of the excitation energy set the direction of net energy flow. Pairs containing the polar H2O guest, with λ above 40 cm−1, lie in the incoherent regime, whereas O2@C60, 5750 cm−1 below the other cages, is isolated from them. Two-dimensional electronic spectra of the all-system endohedral fullerenes show beats at the exciton gaps and spectral diffusion on the 100 fs time scale of the bath. We further demonstrate that this mapping can be inverted. A feed-forward neural network trained on a corpus of 3000 HEOM trajectories recovers a dimer’s site-energy gap, excitonic coupling and λ from a single 2 ps trace, with mean absolute errors of 3.45, 1.87 and 1.13 cm−1 on 600 unseen realisations. The coherence must accompany the population, because the sign of the coupling is reversed by a gauge transformation that leaves the populations unchanged; supplied with ρ12(t), the network recovers it in every held-out case. Internalising the bath thus renders coherence both tunable by design and readable from the dynamics.

item.title: Machine Learning for Ionic Conductivity Prediction in Polymer Electrolytes: A Benchmark on Lithium Systems and a Feasibility Study on the Data-Scarce Multivalent (Mg, Zn, Na) Frontier
item.description: Solid and gel polymer electrolytes are central to safer, more flexible batteries, and machine learning has been used to predict their ionic conductivity directly from composition and processing variables. Almost all of this work targets lithium-ion systems, for which large, curated datasets exist. Polymer electrolytes conducting multivalent or non-lithium cations (magnesium, zinc, sodium) are promising lower-cost alternatives but remain comparably underexplored, in part because no public, ML-ready dataset of their measured ionic conductivities exists. Here we validate a standard composition-to-conductivity pipeline (Random Forest and XGBoost regression) on OBELiX, a published dataset of 599 lithium solid-state electrolytes, reaching R2 = 0.79 against a mean-predicting baseline near zero. We then construct, to our knowledge, the first ML-ready dataset of Mg-, Zn-, and Na-conducting polymer electrolytes, systematically mined from the primary and review literature: 135 data points across 105 distinct host-polymer/salt systems. Applying the same pipeline to this new dataset, a tuned Random Forest reaches R2 = 0.47 under leave-one-out cross-validation, or 0.36 under a more conservative 5-fold estimate, well below the lithium benchmark.Through chemistry-informed feature engineering and a nested cross-validation check, we show this gap is driven primarily by data scarcity and literature measurement heterogeneity, not by model or feature choice. We argue the scarcity is itself the central finding: it puts a number, for the first time, on how far behind the multivalent and non-lithium polymer electrolyte literature sits relative to the lithium-ion mainstream. We release the curated dataset and pipeline to support future community data collection.

item.title: Effect of Cyclodextrin Type on the Photopolymerization and Network Properties of Oligo(L-lactide)-Extended Poly(ethylene glycol) Formulations
item.description: Cyclodextrins (CDs) are widely used as supramolecular components to provide a platform for designing material properties through non-covalent interactions. In this study, we report how the CD type influences the photopolymerization and network properties of a methacrylated telechelic oligo(L-lactide)-extended poly(ethylene glycol) precursor (PLA-PEG-PLA), denoted MPL with three different cyclodextrins (α-CD, β-CD and 2-hydroxypropyl-β-CD (HP-β-CD)) prepared at a 1:2 MPL:CD molar feed ratio. The effect of cyclodextrin type on the chemical structure, inclusion geometry, thermal behaviour, and physicochemical properties of the resulting material, as well as on their photopolymerization process, was systematically studied using FTIR spectroscopy, 1D and 2D proton (ROESY/NOESY) 1H NMR techniques, and differential scanning calorimetry. Molecular docking was used to visualize plausible inclusion geometries. The influence of photoinitiator type and concentration on polymerisation efficiency was examined, and the cytocompatibility of the cured materials was assessed against L929 fibroblasts. The results showed that the nature of cyclodextrin affects the strength of supramolecular association and systematically influences photo-initiated polymerization kinetics, network formation, and macroscopic material properties. Overall, this work highlights the design of cyclodextrin-mediated supramolecular macromonomer materials and outlines their potential as a tunable photo-curable host-guest polymer network.

item.title: ICl-Mediated Iodocyclization of Electron-Deficient 1,5-Enynes to Functionalized Iodonaphthalenes
item.description: Iodine-induced cyclizations of 1,5-enynes are generally limited to electron-rich alkenes. We report an ICl-mediated iodocyclization of 1,5-enynes bearing strongly electron-withdrawing vinyl-bis(perfluoroalkanesulfonyl)amide groups. A range of aryl-substituted enynes cyclized under mild conditions to give iodonaphthalenes in good yields with tolerance of halogen and carbonyl substituents. The products retain both the iodine atom and the bis(perfluoroalkanesulfonyl)amide unit. Suzuki-Miyaura coupling at the iodine site proceeds without cleavage of the sulfonimide moiety, demonstrating the utility of the products as precursors to functionalized naphthalenes.

item.title: Functional-Group Effects in Biopolymer Binders for Sodium-Ion Battery Electrodes: Interfaces, Rheology, and Electrochemical Performance
item.description: Binders, though typically only a few weight percent of a battery electrode, play an outsized role in determining cell performance and sustainability. Water-soluble green binders have emerged as eco-friendly alternatives that enable aqueous slurry processing and easier recyclability. In this work, we leverage biopolymer-based binders (CMC/SBR, Guar Gum and ι-carrageenan) in sodium-ion battery electrodes (Prussian white cathodes and hard carbon anodes) to demonstrate a new paradigm of sustainable electrode design. Our findings highlight that biopolymer binders (Guar Gum and ι-carrageenan) can effectively “glue” sodium-ion battery electrodes together forming a robust structural network and refine the composition of the passivation layer on electrode interface through the functional groups (hydroxyl, carboxyl, and sulfate bonding). By replacing conventional binders with these green alternatives, high-capacity retention and rate capability were achieved when paired with hard carbon electrodes, all with the added benefits of aqueous processability and sustainability.

item.title: Atom-precise nanocluster architectures programmed by biomolecular assembly
item.description: Ligand-protected metal nanoclusters hold promise as atomically precise building blocks for nanoscale materials. However, it remains challenging to achieve ligand chemistries that control higher-order organization while still retaining the nanocluster’s atom-precise properties. Here, we present two biomolecular approaches for higher-order organization of silver nanoclusters stabilized by DNA (DNA-AgN). First, using strategies from DNA nanotechnology, we develop complementary DNA-AgN that oligomerize upon toehold-mediated strand displacement reactions. Second, we exploit biotin-streptavidin interactions to oligomerize biotinylated DNA-AgN. Higherorder assembly is confirmed by native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis and cryo-electron microscopy. Optical spectroscopy shows that the nanoclusters retain their optical properties upon assembly, supporting the integrity of their atomically precise structures during biomolecular organization. These results demonstrate the utility of programmable biomolecular interactions for the higher-order assembly of atom-precise inorganic nanoclusters.

item.title: Improving Molecular Dynamics of Aqueous Electrolytes through Data-Driven Sensitivity-Guided GFN2-xTB Reparameterization
item.description: Semiempirical tight-binding methods such as GFN2-xTB enable efficient molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, but their performance is strongly system dependent. The default GFN2-xTB parameterization overestimates equilibrium densities of liquid water and aqueous NaCl, and it underestimates the bond length for Na+–water pairs in the radial distribution function. To correct these deficiencies, we develop a sensitivity-guided stepwise approach to reparameterize GFN2-xTB against cluster-based and periodic revPBE0-D3 data. We find that the GFN2-xTB fitting problem is ill-conditioned, with many compensating parameter changes that reduce fitted errors but yield unphysical densities in MD simulations. Fisher information matrix (FIM) analysis reveals that only a few parameter combinations dominate the sensitivity of fitted observables, suggesting a reduction of the parameter space for efficient optimization. Optimizing those FIM-selected parameter subsets first for H/O and then for Na improves the equilibrium densities and shifts Na+ hydration distances into the experimental ranges without compromising the remaining properties. We achieve these improvements without directly fitting densities or hydration distances. While the best agreement with experiment for densities is achieved by optimizations on periodic datasets that include virials in the objective function, inclusion of targeted scans of essential geometric degrees of freedom in either a periodic or cluster dataset also improves optimization. Our results identify cluster data as a practical route to correct ion-solvation structure via inexpensive reference calculations, while periodic virials provide complementary control over bulk properties. These findings demonstrate that sensitivity-guided parameter selection, combined with carefully selected reference data describing the relevant interactions, enables GFN2-xTB reparameterizations whose improvements in the static fit translate to bulk MD and provides a general strategy for improving dynamical properties from low-cost electronic structure methods.

item.title: Mechanical versus thermal amorphization of ZIF-4: from local rearrangements to network disorder
item.description: There is mounting evidence that different amorphization routes can produce metalorganic framework (MOF) glasses with distinct structures and properties, yet the microscopic origins of these differences remain difficult to establish experimentally. Focusing on the two main synthesis methods, which are melt-quenching and ball-milling, we use molecular dynamics simulations with a machine-learning interatomic potential to compare different glasses obtained from ZIF-4. While both routes largely preserve tetrahedral zinc coordination, mechanical deformation generally produces more distorted local environments, showing that average coordination numbers alone do not capture the structural differences between these glasses. At smaller applied strain, mechanical glasses retain substantial memory of the crystalline network topology, despite pronounced changes in ring geometry. Larger strains erase this topological memory, yielding ring-size distributions similar to those of melt-quenched glasses, while differences in local geometry and porosity persist. Simulations of larger systems reveal a heterogeneous amorphization mechanism, involving the formation and growth of disordered domains. These findings from in silico amorphization support process-dependent polyamorphism in ZIF glasses and identify local geometry, topological memory, and spatial heterogeneity as complementary features needed to characterize their structure and understand the influence of mechanical processing.

item.title: Electrochemically-driven dynamic surface chemistry breaks the selectivity-conversion tradeoff in the oxidative coupling of methane
item.description: The partial oxidation of methane to C2 products such as ethylene (C2H4) and ethane (C2H6) is a notoriously challenging catalytic reaction since the key properties, namely the C2 selectivity and CH4 conversion, scale inversely with each other. Despite decades of research on catalyst design, this fundamental C2 selectivity-CH4 conversion tradeoff remains a preeminent challenge.1 While traditional thermochemical catalyst design approaches seem inadequate to surmount said challenge, the electrochemical oxidative coupling of methane (EOCM) presents an alternative approach to enhance catalytic performance by dynamically altering the working state of the catalyst. In this study, we use (La, Sr)1-xTiO3±δ as a model system to demonstrate how electrochemistry enables one to dynamically tune the surface chemistry for enhancing C2 selectivity. Depending on the bulk composition, we observe either step changes in C2 selectivity or even a continuously increasing C2 selectivity trend by using La0.24Sr0.60TiO3-δ: this composition, once electrochemically activated, can break the traditional OCM tradeoff. We demonstrate that any C2 selectivity enhancement effects are determined by the surface La/Ti and Sr/Ti ratios which dynamically evolve under electrocatalytic conditions. The enrichment of La at these surfaces is central to enhanced C2 selectivity values and is crucially modulated by both the initial surface and bulk composition. The results presented herein highlight the potential of electrochemical materials activation for overcoming traditional challenges in partial methane oxidation and provide guidance on materials design for maximizing the C2 selectivity of EOCM.

item.title: IMPECCABLE: A Digital Twin Drug Discovery Workflow Comprising AI, Physics and Experiment & the Creation of Nanomolar-Potent Inhibitors
item.description: The traditional drug discovery process is slow, costly and prone to high failure rates. To address this, we have developed IMPECCABLE, an integrated, heterogeneous in silico workflow combining physics-based methods and artificial intelligence to explore small-molecule chemical space. Operating on Frontier and Aurora exascale supercomputers, the workflow rapidly screens, generates and evaluates candidate compounds. Promising candidates enter a generative, multi-objective active learning loop where reliable binding free energies from ESMACS and TIES guide REINVENT to predict diverse, novel and synthesizable molecules. Unlike conventional approaches, this tightly coupled architecture integrates hit identification together with hit-to-lead optimisation and expansion within a single automated pipeline. Crucially, and uniquely, IMPECCABLE also integrates human medicinal chemistry input based on experiments, creating a molecular digital twin. We applied IMPECCABLE to two disease-related targets, WDR91 and TNKS2, demonstrating its ability to produce viable binders, while also performing prospective experimental validation for WDR91. Following multi-objective optimisation via an iterative REINVENT-TIES cycle, we identified four potent hits for WDR91 exhibiting nanomolar binding affinity with KD values between 129 ± 1 nM and 287 ± 1 nM. Remarkably, these four hits emerged from a selection of just ten synthesized compounds, demonstrating an exceptional ca 40% success rate.

item.title: Interfacial Engineering of 2D/2D BiVO4/V2CTx Heterostructures for Enhanced Symmetric Supercapacitor Performance Across Various Electrolytes
item.description: Engineering well-defined heterostructured composites is an effective strategy for improving the electrochemical performance of energy storage systems. In this study, a 2D/2D BiVO4/V2CTx heterostructure was synthesized via a simple hydrothermal method and, for the first time, systematically tested as a symmetric supercapacitor electrode in neutral (1 M Na2SO4), alkaline (1 M KOH), and acidic (1 M H2SO4) electrolytes. The composite showed better electrochemical performance compared to pristine V2CTx, with specific capacitances of 191.5 F g-1, 107 F g-1, and 239 F g-1 in Na2SO4, KOH, and H2SO4, respectively, at 0.016 A g-1. A high energy density of 83.3 Wh kg-1 at 147.5 W kg-1 was achieved in the neutral electrolyte, along with excellent rate capability and Coulombic efficiency. These improvements arise from the synergistic interaction between BiVO4 and V2CTx, which increases active site accessibility and promotes efficient ion and electron transport. Overall, the results show that the BiVO4/V2CTx heterostructure is a promising and versatile electrode material for high-performance supercapacitors.

item.title: Beyond heuristics: structure-aware screening reveals the limits of composition-based cathode design
item.description: Composition-level heuristics based on transition-metal identity are widely used to anticipate lithium-ion cathode durability, but their physical basis is rarely tested against structure-resolved data. Screening 2,774 Li insertion electrodes from the Materials Project, we compare a metal-identity heuristic with a transparent Degradation Screening Index (DSI) built from three structure-resolved descriptors: delithiation volume strain, charged-phase energy above hull and band gap. Against 11 experimentally characterised cathodes the DSI ranks durability better (Spearman ρ = 0.76, p = 0.007) than the metal-identity heuristic (ρ = 0.55, p = 0.08) or a single volume-strain descriptor (ρ = 0.55, p = 0.08), and at database scale the heuristic correlates only weakly with the DSI (ρ = 0.37, n = 787). Resolving LiCuO2 into its polymorph-specific electrode entries shows delithiation strain from 4.7 to 47% and DSI values spanning three of four durability categories at fixed composition. For energy-density prediction, neither compositional descriptors (R2 = 0.39, 132 Magpie features) nor structural descriptors alone (R2 = 0.36; 0.27 under grouped cross-validation) are predictive, and the accuracy of an 8-feature model (R2 = 0.95) is fully accounted for by voltage, capacity and density, the arithmetic constituents of the target; its role is therefore confined to coverage and uncertainty estimation. Multi-objective Pareto analysis over energy density, DSI and supply-chain criticality shows that no single material is universally optimal. All durability estimates are reported as relative DSI categories rather than cycle counts, and structure-resolved descriptors, not composition alone, should anchor durability screening.

item.title: Tribology at the Flip of a Switch: Dynamic Control of Friction and Adhesion with Surface Phonon Polaritons
item.description: Advanced applications of robotics and haptics require the ability to modulate friction and adhesion in a dynamic fashion, in real time. Existing technologies, however, suffer from the need for high voltage circuitry, slow response times, and poor spatial resolution, limiting their utility. Moving away from traditional approaches, here we demonstrate that tuned interfacial interactions involving surface phonon polaritons (SPhPs) can control friction and adhesion in real time at surfaces. SPhPs are hybrid light-matter states formed by the coupling of photons and phonons, which can be excited in polar dielectrics. Since phonon coupling is a primary mechanism for frictional energy dissipation, optically gating SPhPs provides a pathway to controlling this. Moreover, the dipolar nature of the polaritons can modify adhesion in response to localized surface electric field confinement. Here, using atomic force microcopy (AFM), we demonstrate that when SiC thin films are optically pumped in the Reststrahlen (RS) band, the friction and adhesion between a Pt probe tip and a SiC surface can be turned “on” and “off’ with light, with a nearly 3-fold increase in friction and 4-fold increase in adhesion, when illuminated. The influence of SiC film thickness, local interfacial dielectric, and optical excitation energy are described.

item.title: From Catalytic Networks to Activity Landscapes: A Hierarchical Nonequilibrium Framework for Catalysis
item.description: Catalysis is commonly described in terms of free-energy profiles, elementary steps, barriers, intermediates, adsorption energies, turnover frequency (TOF), and selectivity. These quantities are essential, yet they do not fully answer a deeper question: what makes a system catalytic? Here we retain the waterwheel picture for catalysts as an organizing model and develop it into a hierarchical framework connecting microscopic kinetics to macroscopic turnover. In this framework, the established correspondence between productive steady-state flux and TOF is used to recast catalytic performance as a nonequilibrium activity landscape, linking rate constants and catalyst-state populations to observable performance. A catalyst is viewed as a hierarchical system with accessible multistate capacity, regenerative closure, kinetic and thermodynamic compensation, and productive nonequilibrium steadystate (NESS) current. The catalyst provides the structured wheel, while reaction conditions provide the thermodynamic driving force. The framework recovers classical catalytic principles as limiting cases and motivates catalyticity as a condition-dependent capacity defined over an explicitly declared operating or design domain, rather than as a new observable replacing TOF. A literature-inspired Pd(PPh3)4/Pd-PEPPSI Suzuki–Miyaura model illustrates how the framework converts barrier data into NESS currents, ratecontrol coefficients, Hessian modes, frustration indices, and domain-level activity capacities. A Gaussianprocess surrogate and an active-learning workflow further show how sparse evaluations of the activity landscape can reconstruct and navigate such landscapes, suggesting a practical route toward DFT- and experiment-guided catalyst design.

item.title: Uncertainty-Aware Techno-Economic Assessment of Calcium-Based Treatment and Caustic Recovery from Refinery Spent Caustic
item.description: Refinery spent caustic is difficult to treat because of its high alkalinity, sulfur species and dissolved organics. Independent electrolyte-model calculations (PHREEQC; not experimental validation) show that lime treatment cannot both recover caustic and precipitate sulfate as gypsum: gypsum fell below 0.1% of the sulfate once the equilibrium hydroxide exceeded 0.08–0.23 mol/kg (25–90 °C; up to 0.31 with solubility-product shifts of ±0.5 log units), while carbonate causticization stayed favorable (97% conversion at 25 °C, 1 M initial NaOH). Sulfate removal as a solid therefore needs a separate environment from caustic recovery, which defines when neutralization, causticization with recycle or a staged hybrid applies. A Monte Carlo model (10,000 draws; 720 to 1,320 designs) carries this constraint into process design, a sulfate-limited recycle loop and an economic screen against third-party disposal. Oxygen supply is the physical limit: at 80 °C with atmospheric air the required oxygen-transfer rate exceeds the achievable one by a median factor of 23, so the kinetics-only optimum (median NPV $11.7M for Route B, $5.4M for neutralization) is an upper bound. The preferred design is conditional on oxygen enrichment: with 90% oxygen, 60 °C and 12 h, Route B has a median NPV of $6.4M (P10 −$1.3M; P(NPV>0) = 84%) against $0.2M for neutralization, but it meets the sulfide-removal requirement in only 39% of draws without chemical enhancement of transfer and 67% with half the assumed kLa; with air it is not viable. Results are conditional screening values, not forecasts; no experimental data are reported.
